userStories.title: Backend test fixture audit — seed helpers and shared setup
userStories.description:
Audit and consolidate backend test fixture setup. Create reusable seed helpers in `backend/src/test-helpers/seed.ts` so test files don't re-implement workspace/user/billing creation inline. Ensure all tests use the shared `query()` helper and the test database is migrated before tests run. ALWAYS run tests with `--verbose --runInBand` flags, never bare `npm test`.

## Context
- **seed.ts pattern**: Use `query<T>()` from `backend/src/db/index.ts` for all inserts — return the inserted row via `RETURNING *`. Use `$1, $2, ...` numbered placeholders. Each helper should accept a `Partial<T>` overrides argument merged with sensible defaults (e.g. `seedWorkspace({ label: 'test-ws' })`).

- **globalSetup / globalTeardown**: `jest.config.ts` `globalSetup` must import and invoke the pg-index migration runner against `DATABASE_URL` (ensure it points to a test DB, e.g. `rorca_test`). `globalTeardown` should `TRUNCATE` in reverse FK order or use `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE` — never `DROP` tables (that would require re-running migrations on next run).

- **Pool lifecycle gotcha**: `globalSetup` and `globalTeardown` run in separate worker processes from tests — they cannot share the pool singleton from `db/index.ts` directly. Open a fresh `pg.Pool` scoped to the setup/teardown file and call `pool.end()` after the migration/truncate. Test files themselves use the shared pool from `db/index.ts` and must call `pool.end()` in `afterAll()` to avoid Jest hanging.

- **AGE search_path hygiene**: If any seed helper touches graph tables or calls `setupAgeSession()`, restore `SET search_path = rorca, public` before releasing the connection — otherwise subsequent test queries will hit `ag_catalog.workspaces` (empty) and produce silent 404-style failures.

- **Migration runner idempotency**: The pg-index migration runner uses `schema_migrations` to skip already-applied files — so running it in `globalSetup` against a pre-migrated test DB is safe. New migration files must use timestamp format (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`), not sequential numbers, to avoid collision with existing 001–079 files.

- **Billing seed helpers**: `seedBillingActive()` and `seedBillingTrial(daysRemaining)` must insert into the `billing` table (Stripe subscription tracking). Check column names match the actual schema before writing — the table was added by rorca-billing-launch stories and column names may differ from the ORM-style guesses.

- **Test run flags**: Per acceptance criteria, always invoke Jest as `npx jest --verbose --runInBand` (or `--testPathPattern=<name> --verbose --runInBand`). Never rely on bare `npm test` in verification steps — the `--runInBand` flag is critical to prevent connection pool exhaustion across parallel workers (`PG_POOL_SIZE=1` is set in the jest config for this reason).
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/src/test-helpers/seed.ts` exports: `seedWorkspace(overrides?)`, `seedUser(overrides?)`, `seedBillingActive()`, `seedBillingTrial(daysRemaining)`, `seedPipelineRun(workspaceId, overrides?)` — each inserts via `query()` and returns the inserted row
`backend/jest.config.ts` `globalSetup` runs migration runner against test database before all tests
`backend/jest.config.ts` `globalTeardown` truncates all tables after all tests complete
All test files that had inline `INSERT INTO workspaces` SQL replaced with `seedWorkspace()` calls
All test files that had inline `INSERT INTO users` SQL replaced with `seedUser()` calls
No test file creates its own database connection — all use `query()` from `backend/src/db/index.ts`
Verify with: `npx jest --testPathPattern=seed --verbose --runInBand` exits 0
userStories.notes: Completed manually — seed.ts created, jest.config.ts already had globalSetup/globalTeardown

userStories.title: GitHub Actions CI workflow — test run on every PR
userStories.description:
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the backend test suite and type-checks on every PR. Post a comment with test results summary. Use PostgreSQL 16 service container. ALWAYS run tests with `--verbose --runInBand --ci` flags.

## Context
- **PostgreSQL service container port**: Use `5433` (not default 5432) — matches `DATABASE_URL=postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca_test`. Set `options: --port 5433` on the service container and map `ports: ['5433:5432']` so the container's internal 5432 maps to host 5433.
- **Test flags are non-negotiable**: `--ci --verbose --runInBand --json --outputFile=test-results.json` must all be present. `--runInBand` is critical — backend Jest config uses `maxWorkers: 1` (serial execution, PG_POOL_SIZE=1); parallel runners will cause DB pool conflicts.
- **Wait for Postgres readiness**: Add a health-check step before running tests — `pg_isready -h localhost -p 5433 -U rorca` in a retry loop, or use `options: --health-cmd "pg_isready" --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5` on the service container.
- **PR comment deduplication**: The `actions/github-script` step must search existing comments for `[CI Test Results]` marker and call `updateComment` if found, `createComment` if not. Skipping this check duplicates comments on every re-run.
- **`test-results.json` parsing**: Jest `--json` output has shape `{ numTotalTests, numPassedTests, numFailedTests, numPendingTests, testResults[] }`. Parse with `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('backend/test-results.json', 'utf8'))` inside the `github-script` step — note the path is relative to repo root.
- **Two separate `npx tsc --noEmit` calls**: One from repo root (frontend typecheck) and one from `backend/` — the acceptance criteria lists both. Use `working-directory` on the step or explicit `cd` in run commands; don't merge them into one.
- **Node.js 22 cache**: Use `cache: 'npm'` with `cache-dependency-path: '**/package-lock.json'` on the `actions/setup-node` step to cache both root and backend `node_modules` independently.
- **Exit code propagation**: GitHub Actions will fail automatically if `npm test` exits non-zero, but ensure the `github-script` comment step runs even on failure — use `if: always()` so test results are posted even when tests fail.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `.github/workflows/ci.yml` created
Workflow triggers on: `push` to `main`, `pull_request` targeting `main`

Workflow steps: checkout, setup Node.js 22, cache node_modules, `npm ci`, `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `cd backend && npm test -- --ci --verbose --runInBand --json --outputFile=test-results.json`
PostgreSQL 16 service container with `POSTGRES_DB=rorca_test`, `POSTGRES_USER=rorca`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=rorca`, `POSTGRES_PORT=5433`
After test run: `actions/github-script` step posts PR comment with `[CI Test Results]` marker — shows total/passed/failed/skipped counts
PR comment is edited on re-runs (not duplicated) — searches for existing `[CI Test Results]` comment
Workflow fails with exit code 1 if any test fails
`DATABASE_URL=postgres://rorca:rorca@localhost:5433/rorca_test` set in workflow env

userStories.title: End-to-end smoke test script — full user journey verification
userStories.description:
Create a smoke test script `backend/scripts/smoke-test.ts` that verifies the complete Rorca user journey on a fresh installation: register workspace → generate spec → approve → trigger run → verify completion. Run before any public release.

## Context
- **Script location & runner**: Place at `backend/scripts/smoke-test.ts`; run with `npx tsx backend/scripts/smoke-test.ts`. No Jest/Vitest involved — this is a standalone script with direct `fetch()` calls to `http://localhost:3030`.
- **Auth middleware is globally disabled** — no Authorization header needed for any API calls (intentional, local tool per CLAUDE.md). All endpoints are open.
- **Spec `id` = filename slug, not human title** — after `POST /api/specs/generate`, extract `spec.id` (slug) from the response to construct subsequent calls (`/api/specs/:id/approve`, `/api/pipeline/trigger`). Do NOT use `spec.specName` or `spec.title` as the path segment.
- **Pipeline trigger returns `{ queued: true, runId }` immediately** — the run only executes if the pg-boss Worker process is running (`npm run worker`). Smoke test should fail fast with a clear message if worker heartbeat is stale (`GET /api/pipeline/worker/health` or check `worker_heartbeat.last_seen > 90s`).
- **Poll for `status = 'done'`** — valid terminal statuses are `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`. Poll `GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId` (not `/stories`). If status hits `failed` or `cancelled` before `done`, exit code 1 immediately rather than waiting the full 10 minutes.
- **`/tmp/rorca-smoke-test` must exist as a git repo** — `POST /api/workspaces` registers a path and likely validates it's a git repository. Create a bare git repo (`git init /tmp/rorca-smoke-test`) before Step 1, or the workspace registration will fail.
- **Cleanup only on success** — per acceptance criteria, leave the workspace row and `/tmp/rorca-smoke-test` intact on failure to aid debugging. Use a `try/finally` guard carefully: cleanup block only runs if a `success` flag was set.
- **Error output clarity**: Each step should print the HTTP status + response body snippet on failure so the operator knows exactly which step failed and why (not just `✗ Step 4`).
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/scripts/smoke-test.ts` — runnable with `npx tsx backend/scripts/smoke-test.ts`
Requires `DATABASE_URL` env var; uses `SPEC_PROVIDER=claude` by default
Step 1: POST /api/workspaces — register test workspace at `/tmp/rorca-smoke-test`; assert 201
Step 2: POST /api/specs/generate — generate 2-story spec with brief 'Add a hello world endpoint'; assert 2 userStories
Step 3: POST /api/specs/:id/approve — approve spec; assert file moved to approved/
Step 4: POST /api/pipeline/trigger — trigger run; assert `{ queued: true, runId }` returned
Step 5: Poll GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId every 5s for up to 10 minutes; assert `status = 'done'`
Step 6: GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/stories — assert at least 1 story has `status = 'pass'`
Script prints ✓/✗ for each step; exits code 0 on full success, code 1 on any failure
Cleanup: deletes test workspace row and removes `/tmp/rorca-smoke-test` on success only

userStories.title: Fix billing test failures
userStories.description:
Fix all failing tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/billing.test.ts`. Common issues: Stripe SDK not mocked, missing `billing` table columns from recent migrations, `requirePlan` middleware not imported correctly. ALWAYS run with: `npx jest --testPathPattern=billing --verbose --runInBand` to verify. Never run bare `npm test`.

## Context
- **Run command is non-negotiable**: Always use `npx jest --testPathPattern=billing --verbose --runInBand` — `--runInBand` is required because Jest config sets `maxWorkers: 1` (serial) and billing tests share DB state; bare `npm test` risks parallel interference
- **Stripe mock placement**: `jest.mock('../../../lib/stripe-client')` must appear at the top of the test file before any imports that transitively import `stripe-client`; if `stripe-client.ts` uses a singleton pattern, ensure the mock factory resets between tests with `beforeEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks())`
- **Seed all new billing columns**: Test setup must include `trial_ends_at`, `license_key`, `activated_at`, `stripe_customer_id`, `stripe_subscription_id`, `plan_checked_at` in INSERT statements — missing columns cause silent `undefined` reads that break assertions without clear errors
- **`stripe_webhook_events` table must exist in test DB**: Idempotency tests require the table to be seeded; check that the migration creating it has run (timestamp-prefix migration — look in `pg-migrations/` for the relevant file) and that test setup truncates it in `beforeEach` to avoid state bleed
- **`requirePlan` middleware bypass pattern**: Tests that don't exercise billing gates should mock `requirePlan` as a passthrough — `jest.mock('../../../lib/requirePlan', () => ({ requirePlan: () => (req, res, next) => next() }))`; import path must match exactly what `billing.ts` route file uses
- **DB pool cleanup in `afterAll`**: Billing tests must call `pool.end()` or equivalent in `afterAll()` — per engineering standards, always clean up DB pool connections to prevent Jest from hanging after test completion
- **AppError subclasses for billing errors**: Any billing route error assertions should expect `{ error: string, code?: string }` shape (not raw `message`), matching the centralized `errorHandler` serialization pattern — use `ConflictError` (409) for duplicate webhook events, `UnprocessableError` (422) for invalid Stripe payloads
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern=billing --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
Stripe SDK is mocked via `jest.mock('../../../lib/stripe-client')` — no live API calls
All new billing columns (`trial_ends_at`, `license_key`, `activated_at`, `stripe_customer_id`, `stripe_subscription_id`, `plan_checked_at`) are present in test seed data
`requirePlan` middleware is correctly mocked or bypassed in tests that don't test billing gates
Webhook idempotency tests use the `stripe_webhook_events` table (seeded in test setup)

userStories.title: Fix pipeline test failures
userStories.description:
Fix all failing tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/pipeline.test.ts` and related pipeline test files. Common issues: pg-boss not mocked, stale column names (`triggered_via`, `queue_position`, `last_heartbeat`), worker concurrency lock queries failing. ALWAYS run with: `npx jest --testPathPattern=pipeline --verbose --runInBand`.

## Context
- **Run command is non-negotiable**: Always `npx jest --testPathPattern=pipeline --verbose --runInBand` — the `--runInBand` flag is critical since backend tests use `maxWorkers: 1` (serial execution) and share a single `PG_POOL_SIZE=1` connection; parallel runs will deadlock on the pool.

- **Mock pg-boss completely**: `jest.mock('pg-boss')` at the top of each test file — the worker process (`worker.ts`) is a separate process that must NOT be invoked during tests. Any `boss.send()`, `boss.work()`, or `boss.start()` calls hitting a real pg-boss instance will fail with connection errors or attempt real DB operations.

- **Required columns in pipeline_runs fixtures**: Test fixtures and mock `queryOne`/`query` return values must include all columns added by recent migrations: `queue_position` (INT), `last_heartbeat` (TIMESTAMPTZ), `plan_checked_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ), `plan_at_trigger` (BOOLEAN), `triggered_via` (TEXT). Missing columns cause TypeScript strict-mode errors or silent `undefined` comparisons that break assertions.

- **Worker concurrency query shape**: The concurrency check `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE workspace_id=$1 AND status='running'` returns `{ count: string }` (PostgreSQL COUNT always returns text) — mock DB responses must use `{ count: '0' }` not `{ count: 0 }` or the `parseInt()` call will behave unexpectedly.

- **`run_output_chunks` queries**: Any pipeline route that writes or reads output chunks needs the mock DB to handle `INSERT INTO run_output_chunks` and `SELECT ... FROM run_output_chunks` — either mock the `execute()` helper to swallow inserts or seed the mock with the correct `(run_id, sequence, data)` shape.

- **Pool cleanup in `afterAll()`**: Per the testing standard, always call `pool.end()` or equivalent in `afterAll()` — failing to do so leaves the PG pool open and causes Jest to hang after tests complete ("Jest did not exit one second after the test run has completed").

- **`triggered_via` is `z.string().nullish()`**: The WAL schema null-rejection fix from 2026-03-12 applies here — Zod schemas for pipeline payloads must use `.nullish()` not `.optional()` for nullable DB columns, or test payloads that omit these fields will fail Zod validation before hitting the mock DB layer.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern=pipeline --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
pg-boss is mocked via `jest.mock('pg-boss')` — no real queue operations in tests
All new pipeline_runs columns present in test fixtures: `queue_position`, `last_heartbeat`, `plan_checked_at`, `plan_at_trigger`, `triggered_via`
Worker concurrency check (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE workspace_id=$1 AND status='running'`) is correctly handled in mocked DB responses
`run_output_chunks` table queries are mocked or seeded correctly
0 failures in all pipeline test files

userStories.title: Fix auth and users test failures
userStories.description:
Fix all failing tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/auth.test.ts` and `users.test.ts`. Common issues: JWT secret not set in test env, refresh token table schema changes, GitHub OAuth scope column missing. ALWAYS run with: `npx jest --testPathPattern='auth|users' --verbose --runInBand`.

## Context
- **Run command is non-negotiable**: Always use `npx jest --testPathPattern='auth|users' --verbose --runInBand` — `--runInBand` forces serial execution (matches `maxWorkers: 1` Jest config) and prevents pool connection race conditions between test files.

- **JWT_SECRET must be in test environment**: Check `backend/jest.env.ts` or the Jest `globalSetup` file — if missing, all JWT sign/verify calls throw and every auth test fails. Add `process.env.JWT_SECRET = 'test-secret'` (or similar) there, not in individual test files.

- **Schema drift is the primary suspect**: The `refresh_tokens` table has evolved across migrations (001–079+ sequential + any new timestamp-format files). Run `\d refresh_tokens` against the test DB to confirm columns match what the route handlers expect. Missing columns (e.g. `user_agent`, `ip_address`, `revoked_at`) cause silent insert failures or query errors.

- **`github_connections.scope` column**: Added by BL-014 migration — confirm this migration ran in the test DB. If tests spin up a fresh schema, the migration runner in `pg-index.ts` must have processed all migrations including BL-014 before the test suite starts.

- **GitHub OAuth mocks must match exact response shape**: The callback handler likely calls `https://api.github.com/user` and `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` — mocks must return the exact fields the handler destructures (e.g. `id`, `login`, `email`, `name`). A mock returning a partial object causes TypeScript-invisible runtime destructuring failures.

- **DB pool cleanup in `afterAll()`**: Per testing standards, every test file must call `pool.end()` (or the project's equivalent pool teardown) in `afterAll()`. Missing this causes Jest to hang after tests pass, or connection leaks that corrupt subsequent test files run in the same process.

- **Auth middleware is globally disabled in production** (`server.ts` line ~78) but test routes may import middleware directly — verify test setup doesn't accidentally re-enable global `authRequired`, which would cause all non-auth routes to 401.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern='auth|users' --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
`JWT_SECRET` is set in `backend/jest.env.ts` or test globalSetup
All `refresh_tokens` table columns match current migration schema
`github_connections` table has `scope` column (from BL-014 migration)
GitHub OAuth callback tests mock the GitHub API response correctly
0 failures in auth and users test files

userStories.title: Fix specs and direction test failures
userStories.description:
Fix all failing tests in `backend/src/routes/__tests__/specs.test.ts`, `direction.test.ts`, and related files. Common issues: `wal_events.ts` column (`ts` not `created_at`), spec path construction, kanban query failures. ALWAYS run with: `npx jest --testPathPattern='specs|direction|wal' --verbose --runInBand`.

## Context
- **WAL column is `ts`, not `created_at`**: All `wal_events` queries must use `ORDER BY ts DESC`, `SELECT ts`, and `WHERE ts > ...`. Tests that mock or query `wal_events` must reflect this. The column alias `ts AS created_at` is only for API consumers, not raw SQL.
- **Spec path pattern**: Tests must construct paths as `forge/specs/approved/<slug>.json` (NOT `specs/approved/<specName>.json`). The `id` field is always the filename slug; `specName` is display-only. Backend resolves full path via `path.join(workspace.path, specPath)`.
- **Kanban endpoint shape**: `GET /api/specs/kanban` returns cards with `activeRunStatus?: 'running' | 'queued'` and `queuePosition?: number` fields. Tests asserting kanban response shape must include these optional fields or use partial matchers — missing them will cause assertion failures.
- **Direction layer schema**: `direction_layers` stores content keyed by `(workspace_id, layer, domain)`. Tests must seed with valid layer values (`L1`–`L5`) and not assume a `created_at` column exists unless confirmed in migrations.
- **DB helpers use numbered placeholders**: All test fixtures or route assertions that construct SQL must use `$1, $2, ...` (not `?`). `queryOne<T>()` returns `T | undefined`, not `T` — tests asserting on results must handle the undefined case.
- **Run test command exactly as specified**: `npx jest --testPathPattern='specs|direction|wal' --verbose --runInBand` — `--runInBand` is critical because the backend Jest config sets `maxWorkers: 1` (serial) and `PG_POOL_SIZE=1`; parallel test runs will cause connection pool contention and flaky failures.
- **`afterAll` pool cleanup required**: Any test file that imports the DB pool must call `pool.end()` in `afterAll()` to avoid Jest hanging after tests complete. Missing cleanup is a common source of test timeouts.
- **AppError hierarchy for error assertions**: Tests checking error responses should expect `{ error: string, code?: string, details?: ... }` shape (not raw `message` fields). Route handlers throw `ValidationError`/`NotFoundError` etc.; the centralized `errorHandler` serializes them.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern='specs|direction|wal' --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
All `wal_events` queries in tests use `ts` column (not `created_at`)
Spec path construction in tests uses `forge/specs/approved/<slug>.json` pattern
Direction layer tests use correct `direction_layers` schema
Kanban endpoint tests account for `activeRunStatus` and `queuePosition` fields
0 failures in specs, direction, and WAL test files

userStories.title: Fix workspace, skills, and analytics test failures
userStories.description:
Fix all failing tests in workspace, skills, and analytics test files. Common issues: AGE search_path pool poisoning in tests, missing workspace columns, echolocation health score changes. ALWAYS run with: `npx jest --testPathPattern='workspace|skills|analytics' --verbose --runInBand`.

## Context
- **AGE search_path restoration is critical**: Any test that triggers graph/AGE queries must restore `SET search_path = rorca, public` after each test case — use `afterEach` hooks. The pool `on('connect')` guard in `db/index.ts` is a safety net only, not a substitute. Poisoned connections cause intermittent "Workspace not found" 404s that appear as unrelated test failures.

- **Run tests with `--runInBand`**: The Jest config uses `maxWorkers: 1` and serial execution (`PG_POOL_SIZE=1`). Never run workspace/skills/analytics tests in parallel — shared DB pool connections will interleave and corrupt search_path state.

- **`token_usage` column names**: Query the actual `token_usage` table schema before writing analytics test assertions. Column name mismatches are a known failure pattern — verify against the migration files in `backend/src/db/pg-migrations/` before asserting on specific field names.

- **Skills endpoints must be fully mocked**: `POST /api/skills/install-from-sh` fetches from `skills.sh` and then GitHub raw URLs — both must be intercepted with `jest.spyOn` or `nock`. No live network calls in tests. The install chain has 4 fallback steps (search → two raw URL patterns → GitHub tree API), so ensure mocks cover all paths or stub at the HTTP client level.

- **Workspace endpoint coverage gaps**: Ensure `env-vars`, `budget`, `agent-hooks`, and `agent-profiles` sub-routes all have at minimum a happy-path GET test. These are often added in migrations without corresponding test additions — check `backend/src/routes/workspaces.ts` against existing test files to identify gaps.

- **`echolocation` health scores are threshold-sensitive**: `workspace-echolocation.ts` computes weighted scores (CLAUDE.md 30pt, AGENTS.md 20pt, etc.) with half-credit penalties for short files. Test fixture workspaces must satisfy these thresholds or assertions on health score ranges will flake — either use fixed fixture files with known content lengths or assert `>= 0` bounds rather than exact values.

- **`AppError` hierarchy for error assertions**: Tests asserting on error responses should expect `{ error: string, code?: string, details? }` shape. Raw `throw new Error()` will produce a 500 without a `code` field — use `NotFoundError`, `ValidationError`, etc. from `backend/src/lib/errors.ts` to get deterministic HTTP status codes in test assertions.

- **`afterAll` pool cleanup required**: Every test file touching the DB must call `pool.end()` or equivalent in `afterAll()` — the Jest config enforces 30s timeout but leaked pool connections will cause the process to hang after tests complete, appearing as a CI timeout failure rather than a test failure.
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern='workspace|skills|analytics' --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
Any test that calls graph/AGE queries restores `SET search_path = rorca, public` after each test
Workspace env-vars, budget, agent-hooks, and agent-profiles endpoints all have corresponding test coverage
Skills install and preview endpoints are mocked (no live skills.sh API calls in tests)
Analytics token usage queries use correct column names from `token_usage` table

userStories.title: Fix worker, lib, and MCP test failures — achieve 0 failures total
userStories.description:
Fix all remaining test failures in worker, lib, and MCP test files. Verify the full suite achieves 0 failures. ALWAYS run targeted: `npx jest --testPathPattern='worker|lib|mcp' --verbose --runInBand`. Final verification: `npx jest --verbose --runInBand --forceExit` (full suite — only run this last).

## Context
- **Test runner config**: Backend tests use Jest with `ts-jest`, `maxWorkers: 1` (serial), 30s timeout, `PG_POOL_SIZE=1` — always run with `--runInBand` to enforce serial execution and avoid pool contention
- **DB pool cleanup critical**: Every test file touching DB must call `pool.end()` or equivalent in `afterAll()` — missing cleanup causes Jest to hang after tests pass, requiring `--forceExit` as a safety net but not a fix
- **Worker heartbeat mocking**: `worker_heartbeat` table writes happen on a 30s interval — mock `setInterval` with `jest.useFakeTimers()` or stub the DB `execute()` call directly; don't let real timers fire during tests
- **AGE search_path hygiene in lib tests**: Any test touching `knowledge-graph.ts`, `graph-context.ts`, or `graph-drift-detector.ts` must mock `setupAgeSession()` or ensure `SET search_path = rorca, public` is restored — otherwise subsequent queries in the same pool connection fail with wrong schema
- **Rate limiter DB mock**: `rate-limiter.ts` reads from `rate_limits` table with a 30s cache — stub `queryOne()` to return `{ max_requests: 100, window_seconds: 60 }` or equivalent; avoid real DB reads in unit tests; set `NODE_ENV=test` (rate limiter skips enforcement unless `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true`)
- **MCP server tests**: MCP tools make HTTP calls to `http://localhost:3030/api/*` — mock with `nock` or `jest.spyOn` on the underlying `fetch`/`axios`; do not start a real Express server in MCP unit tests
- **SSE hub isolation**: `sse-hub.ts` uses a module-level subscriber set — import the hub fresh per test or call the cleanup/unsubscribe returned by `subscribe()` in `afterEach` to prevent cross-test event leakage
- **pg-boss worker tests**: pg-boss `boss.work()` callbacks are async and fire on real DB polling — mock the entire `PgBoss` class (or use `jest.mock('pg-boss')`) rather than relying on timing; the singleton guard check (`worker_heartbeat` conflict detection) should be tested with a mocked `queryOne` returning a recent `last_seen` timestamp
acceptanceCriteria: `npx jest --testPathPattern='worker|lib|mcp' --verbose --runInBand` exits with code 0
Worker heartbeat and singleton guard tests pass with mocked `worker_heartbeat` table
Rate limiter tests correctly mock the `rate_limits` DB table
MCP server tests mock the Express API responses correctly
SSE hub tests use in-process pub/sub (no real HTTP connections)
Final full suite run: `npx jest --verbose --runInBand --forceExit` exits with code 0 and 0 failures
